newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes steady, market seeks incentives.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes steady, market seeks incentives.

text.p: Precious metal prices stayed close to earlier levels on Thursday afternoon as the gold market continued to look for stimulation in its narrow price band.

Dealers said the bearishness of earlier in the week had lifted slightly now that support seemed to have been established at $340 per ounce, at least ahead of next Monday's over-the-counter (OTC) options expiry.
Gold moved narrowly either side of $341 bid to be fixed at $340.90 after $341.15 this morning and Wednesday's $341.00.
The June Comex contract was down $0.60 shortly after the fixing at $342.70.
Activity was generally dampened by holidays, with the Jewish Passover all this week and a week-long Moslem holiday has just finished.
Dealers said there was some protective moves concerning call options accumulated around the $340.00 strike before the expiry.
Even so gold's range for the day so far was a miserly $1.20 between $340.60 and $341.80 with no real trend emerging.

In a Reuters' poll of market analyst conducted earlier this week, eight of ten respondents forecast a higher gold price at the end of the quarter than now. However the mean was only a few dollars above the current price at $345.80.
The forecast was for palladium prices to be lower than currently by end June, mainly on the assumption that Russia would have straightened out its export contracts with Japan by then.
The forecasters placed spot palladium on a mean of $146.90 at June 30 which compared with Thursday's price of $155.50/$156.50, up $1.50.
Most of the platinum attention was on the forward markets with good borrowing interest for short dates which raised one-month lease rates, dealers said.
"A lot of it is because nobody has got the liquidity so people are trading forwards rather than trading on the spots," said the London dealer.
One-month platinum lease jumped to 12.5 percent from around 10 while palladium was available at 14 percent, dealers said.
The prospect of continued delays in PGM shipments from Russia, the world's biggest producer, is buoying the market, but the bubble is expected to burst once talks with Japan resume.
Moscow has yet to set the date to begin talks.
